questions.stem: A HiGHS log of a maximization prints the row ' T     120      35        40  62.50%   1052.5          1040               1.20%      310     25     12      5400     3.1s'. What does it report?

options.text: A node's LP gave a plan worth 1040, and no plan can be worth more than 1052.5
options.says: Right: T is Evaluate node, BestSol 1040 is the new incumbent and BestBound 1052.5 the dual bound.

options.text: A node's LP gave a plan worth 1052.5, and no plan can be worth more than 1040
options.says: The columns are BestBound then BestSol: the bound is 1052.5 and the plan 1040.

options.text: A node's LP left 62.50% of the 120 processed nodes waiting in the queue
options.says: Expl. is the share of the search tree already closed; InQueue, 35, counts the waiting nodes.

options.text: A node's LP kept 1.20% of the 310 cuts in the pool, and dropped the rest
options.says: 1.20% is the gap between bound and incumbent; InLp, 25, counts the cuts in the LP.

origin.section: Each Row of the Table Is a Snapshot of the Search

questions.stem: A maximization's solving report shows Status Optimal, Primal bound 50000, Dual bound 50004 and Gap 0.008% (tolerance: 0.01%). What does Optimal promise about the plan it returns?

options.text: It is worth 50000, and the search proved that no plan is worth more
options.says: A dual bound of 50004 means a plan worth up to 50004 may exist; the search stopped before ruling it out.

options.text: It is worth 50004, since the dual bound is the value it reached
options.says: The dual bound is a limit no plan can beat; the returned plan's value is the primal bound, 50000.

options.text: It is worth 50000, and a plan worth up to 50004 may still exist
options.says: Right: Optimal means the gap is within the tolerance, here 0.008% under 0.01%, not that it is zero.

options.text: It is worth 50000, and the solver stopped at its time limit
options.says: A time limit gives another status; Optimal says the gap reached the tolerance.

origin.section: The Report Is the Verdict, and Optimal Means Within the Gap Tolerance

questions.stem: Partway through the root, a HiGHS log prints '40.0% inactive integer columns, restarting' and then 'Model after restart has 9 rows, 60 cols'. What happened?

options.text: The search failed, and began again from the first LP with nothing kept
options.says: A restart keeps the incumbent and the bound; the rows after it continue from the same values.

options.text: The root fixed many columns, and the smaller model was presolved again
options.says: Right: inactive columns are fixed by the root work, and presolve runs again on what is left.

options.text: The cuts made 40.0% of the rows redundant, and those rows were dropped
options.says: The message counts integer columns, not rows, and they are inactive because they are fixed.

options.text: The model was infeasible, and 40.0% of its columns were relaxed to fix it
options.says: An infeasible model ends with an infeasible status; a restart happens while the search goes on.

origin.section: A Restart Presolves Again With What the Root Learned
